title: Commuting Options & Resources
text:
## General Transportation Announcements
- UMass Boston now offers free e-bike and e-scooter charging at the West Garage Secured Shelter with 13 Saris Power Posts; simply register your bike through Project 529 for Beaconcard access. Learn more about bike parking and facilities .

## Commuting Options & Resources
Transportation Services is committed to providing safe and affordable multi-modal transportation options to all our community members, to reduce traffic congestion and use of single occupancy vehicles (SOV) on campus, and to improve air pollution.

## A Better City TMA
To support our community members and contribute to enhanced quality of life in downtown Boston, UMass Boston is pleased to maintain membership in A Better City Transportation Management Association (TMA). A Better City TMA provides commuter services and citywide advocacy to improve your options for getting around the neighborhood. Join the ABC TMA Network here . At no cost to you, the TMA offers several programs & services to help you navigate transportation options and earn rewards for your commuting choices: Employee Benefits Multimodal trip-planning tool with statewide ride-matching functionality. A Better Commute (ABC): Earn points for your commuting choices (including telecommuting!) and use them to enter raffles. ABC will draw winners every month and grand prizes every quarter! Learn more here . Guaranteed Ride Home (GRH): Earn up to six free Uber rides home per year under qualifying circumstances. Please note - you’ll need to register for this program ahead of time to earn and use your free rides. Learn more here . Bike Check: Earn up to two $25 reimbursements for bike-related expenses every year. Learn more here . Carpool Subsidy: Each rider switching from driving alone to riding in a carpool can earn up to three months of $15 gas cards. Find your carpool crew using GoMass Commute’s ride matching tool! Learn more here . Express Lane: Switch from driving alone to taking an express bus and receive up to three months of $50 reimbursements on your monthly pass. Learn more here . Student Benefits Multimodal trip-planning tool with statewide ride-matching functionality.

## Electric Vehicle Charging
UMass Boston is proud to offer 23 shared ChargePoint EV charging ports across campus, providing convenient and accessible charging for electric vehicles. West Garage (First Floor) : 15 ports. Campus Center Garage (Lower Level) : 4 ports Quad Lot: 4 ports How to Get Started with ChargePoint Step 1: Set Up Your ChargePoint Account Download the ChargePoint App: Available for Android and iOS . Sign Up: Create an account within the app. You can also request a free RFID card during sign-up if you need it for use at other stations in the ChargePoint network. Enroll in Tap to Pay Step 2: How to Charge Your Vehicle Tap your ChargePoint card or your phone using Tap to Pay on the station’s reader symbol to authorize your payment and unlock the plug. To end your session, 4 hours is the limit to charge your vehicle, tap your ChargePoint card or phone on the station’s reader symbol to confirm you want to end your charging session. Remove the charger and return it to the station. Additional Details: Charging costs $0.22 per kWh, with a 4-hour maximum charge per session. Standard parking fees apply in addition to charging costs. Non-charging vehicles parked in EV spaces will be fined $75.

Find information about parking regulations, permit requirements, accessibility, temporary restrictions, and validated guest parking.

## Parking Portal Instructions & Permit Application
All university parking permits must be purchased using the online Parking Portal . The portal may also be used to update your vehicle information and cancel your parking permit. Please log into the portal with your UMass Boston credentials. Apply for a Parking Permit Log into the parking portal and click Permits at the top of the page. In the dropdown, click Get Permits. From there, follow the directions on the screen. Your license plate information must be correct to avoid citations therefore please confirm the accuracy of your license plate information before submitting. Update Vehicle Information Log into the parking portal , and at the top of the page, click Vehicles. If you want to add a vehicle, click Add Vehicle and follow directions on the screen. Please confirm the accuracy of your license plate information before submitting to avoid citations. You then need to add the new vehicle to your permit. First, at the top of the page, click on Permits. Click on your permit number and then at the bottom of the page, click on Add Vehicles To Permit. Select vehicle(s) you wish to add and then click on Add the Selected Vehicle. If you want to delete a vehicle, click on the license plate of the vehicle that you no longer have and at the bottom of the screen click Delete. Cancel Parking Permit Log into the parking portal and click Permits at the top of the page. In the dropdown, click View Permits. From there, click on your permit number. At the bottom of the Permit Details page, please click on the Return Permit button and follow instructions. Cancellation takes effect immediately

## General Parking Permit Rules
UMass Boston Parking Regulations (1/8/24) Permit Requirements: All vehicles parking on campus must hold an active UMass Boston Parking Permit, or use a hourly/daily transient parking ticket upon entry at a gated parking facility, or use the pay by phone option at an ungated facility. Business Day Start Time: The new business day begins at 5:00 A.M. each day in gated and ungated parking facilities. License Plate Display: Permit holders must display a valid state-issued license plate associated when parking on campus. A state-issued license plate must face the aisle from which the parking space was entered. Vehicles without front license plates should not back into spaces in ungated parking facilities. Vehicle Limitation: Permit holders may park only one vehicle on campus at a time. If more than one vehicle is parked on campus at the same time, the permit holder and vehicle will be subject to parking enforcement policies, which may include, warnings, fines, and towing at the permit holder’s cost, and referral to Human Resources or the Dean of Students. Vehicle Information Responsibility: Permit holders are solely responsible for vehicle information on file with Transportation Services. All vehicle information, including registration (license plate), must be entered accurately into the parking permit application. Failure to enter correct information or update information regarding new vehicles, rental vehicles, loaned vehicles, etc. may result in fines and towing. Transferability and ID Requirement: Parking permits are not transferable. The permit holder’s UMass Boston ID (Beacon Card) is required to enter/exit gated parking facilities. A permit holder may appeal a citation within 21 days of issuance if they were issued a citation due to forgetting their Beacon Card. Parking Space Guarantee: Transportation Services guarantees permit holders a parking space on campus but does not guarantee a space near the permit holder’s destination. Parking Regulations Adherence: The unavailability of a specific parking location or space, severe weather, or running late for a class or meeting are not valid excuses for violating any parking regulations. All university parking spaces are clearly identified by either signs or pavement markings. If an area is not specifically marked as university parking, you should assume that you cannot park there. Parking Availability: Parking on campus is limited. All permit types are subject to availability. Responsibility Disclaimer: UMass Boston assumes no responsibility for vehicle damage, theft, or theft of vehicle contents when the vehicle is parked on university property. UMass Boston assumes no responsibility for vehicle damage resulting from towing. Parking Permit Payments: Customer is responsible for full payment of a parking permit that has been purchased. Parking permit must be cancelled to stop payroll deductions or receive pro-rated refund for a permit purchased via credit card or student account.

## Validated Tickets
Validated Guest Parking: University departments who wish to pay for a guest’s parking needs at a gated parking facility are able to purchase pre-paid validated parking tickets. These tickets may only be purchased via a Journal Entry and may be purchased using this form . Usage Locations: Validated tickets can be used at any on campus location (Campus Center, Lot D, or West Garage). Internal Events: When requesting Pre-paid parking, departments looking to request validations for their visitors and events, please use our signup form . External Events: Validations will expire at the conclusion of your event and unused passes may not be returned for a refund. Request Process: To request validations, please use our form . ## Accessible Parking
Accessible parking spaces will be designated by the university in appropriate areas. Parkers will be permitted to park in marked ADA parking spaces where i) the parker has been issued appropriate authorization to park in handicapped spots by the Registry of Motor Vehicles or ii) the parker has been determined by the Human Resources ADA/504 Coordinator office to be entitled to a reasonable parking accommodation.

Construction projects, major university events, and unforeseen emergencies (including weather and snow emergencies) may require Transportation Services to close or restrict gated or ungated lots for a specified period. Transportation Services will notify all affected parking permit holders of the times, dates, and locations of these parking restrictions in advance.

title: Carpool Registration Form
text:

## Parking Fines
The Board of Trustees of the University of Massachusetts, acting under the powers granted by Chapter 75, Section 32A, General Laws of the Commonwealth, hereby adopts subject to the subsequent amendment or revisions contained in Chapters 75 and 90 of the General Laws, the following rules and regulations for the use and operation of vehicles on and about the Boston campus of the university and on other lands of the University associated with the Campus.
Transportation Services keeps official records of all parking ticket violations issued on vehicles. Fines are payable to the University of Massachusetts Boston and collected for the Parking Scholarship Fund.
Under each group are possible fines issuable by the university:
Group A : 101 Parking within HP/DV Space : $150.00 102 Blocking HP Ramp : $150.00 103 Violation of HP Area : $150.00 104 Fraudulent use of a HP placard : $150.00
Group B : 105 Parking within a posted tow zone : $75.00 106 Parking within a posted fire lane : $75.00 107 Parking on a sidewalk : $35.00 108 Parking in a crosswalk: $35.00 109 Parking within 10 feet of a fire hydrant: $35.00 110 Parking within 20 feet of an intersection : $35.00 111 Parking within posted emergency vehicle area: $35.00 112 Obstructing a building exit or entrance: $35.00 113 Parking in controlled area without authorization: $75.00 114 Toll evasion (non-payment of parking fee): $35.00 115 Parking within a posted bus stop: $35.00 116 Parking so as to interfere with snow removal: $35.00 117 Parking in a delivery of service zone: $35.00
Group C : 118 Double parking : $25.00 119 Parking in front of street barricade : $25.00 120 Blocking a driveway : $25.00 121 Blocking a gateway or field entrance: $25.00 122 Parking more than 12 inches from curb: $25.00 123 Parking in no parking zone : $25.00 124 Parking in access lane: $35.00 125 Parking facing the flow of traffic: $25.00 126 Parking on land not for vehicular use: $25.00 127 Parking overnight without authorization: $25.00 128 Parking single vehicle over two parking spaces: $25.00 129 No fine: $0.00

## Parking Enforcement
Transportation Services shall enforce all university parking regulations. In addition, applicable state motor vehicle laws under the Massachusetts vehicle code shall be enforced. Vehicles utilizing the university facilities that are in violation of any section of these regulations will be issued a parking ticket violation and may be towed at the owner’s expense. Parking tickets must be paid or appealed within 21 calendar days of issuance. A person with unpaid parking tickets who fails to pay or appeal the ticket within the time limits prescribed shall have their license and registration sent to the Registry of Motor Vehicles for non-renewal of license and registration. Vehicles that appear to be abandoned on university property may be disposed of in accordance with Commonwealth of Massachusetts statutes. For additional information, you may contact the Parking Clerk by phone: 617.287.7778 or by email: parkingtickets@umb.edu

When receiving a parking ticket violation at the University of Massachusetts Boston you have the right to appeal the violation. Appeals can only be made online at this time. All appeals must be submitted within (21) calendar days from the violation issuance date. You will receive a confirmation email that your appeal has been received. The appeal decision letter will be emailed to the emailed provided within (21) calendar days. All decisions of the Parking Clerk shall be final, subject to any hearing provisions provided by Chapter 90 Section 20A or to judicial review as provided by Chapter 30A Section 14.

## Commute Smarter, Save More
All university parking permits must be purchased using the Parking Portal . The portal may also be used to update your vehicle information and cancel your parking permit. Log in to the portal with your UMass Boston credentials.
The UMass Boston Office of Transportation Services is here to help you access our campus, whether you are coming by car, bus, bike, or foot. Transportation Services is committed to providing safe and affordable multi-modal transportation options to all our community members to reduce traffic congestion and single occupancy vehicles (SOV) on campus, and to improve air pollution.
Use the interactive campus map to find food, vending machines, and other amenities. You can also print our transportation map or find campus buildings on our mobile app
Enrollment Election

## Transit and (Offsite) Parking FSA
Through the Qualified Transportation Benefits Program (QTBP), you are eligible for a pre-tax benefit program that includes both offsite parking and transit related expenses. QTBP is administered by Voya and allows you to have transit and/or offsite parking expenses deducted from your paycheck on a pre-tax basis. Pre-tax limits and reimbursement eligibility are subject to the IRS’s rules and regulations How To Enroll : Employees need to enroll directly through VOYA . If you want to participate in both the Transit and Parking programs you must make elections in each benefit’s section on the election form. How to Change Your Election : You may change or opt out of the program at any point during the plan year. To modify your participation in the plan, you simply access the enrollment form. Once you submit the form, a copy of the request will be sent to Voya and a copy is also sent to your division’s appointed payroll contact, whom will make the necessary updates to payroll to reflect your requested change. *If you are looking for information regarding on-site parking, please visit Umass Boston Transportation Services .

## General Transportation Announcements

## About Biking at UMass Boston
UMass Boston supports cycling as a sustainable transportation option by offering parking , free registration, end-of-trip amenities , and access to the Bluebikes bikeshare program. Whether you bring your own bike or use bikeshare, we provide resources to ensure safe, efficient, and convenient travel on campus.

## How to Park & Register Your Bike

## Where to Park Your Bike (Free & Secure!)
UMass Boston offers over 740 free bike parking spaces campus-wide, including: West Garage Secured Shelter: 125-space indoor, secure bike storage Maintenance Station: Basic maintenance tools are available inside the West Garage Charging Stations (West Garage Bike Shelter Only): 13 Saris Power Posts with 26 ports for e-bikes and e-scooters (free to use with certified batteries). Lock your rear wheel and frame to the ring with a U-lock, then plug in your personal charger. Move your device to another rack once fully charged To use the West Garage secure shelter, you must first register your bicycle through Project 529 . Once your registration is confirmed, you’ll receive access to the shelter using your Beaconcard. Full registration details and instructions are available in Register Your Bike, E-Bike, Scooter, or E-Scooter .

## Register Your Bike, E-Bike, Scooter, or E-Scooter
All bikes, e-bikes, scooters, and e-scooters, can be registered through Project 529. Registration is free, quick, and helps protect your device. Registration is required to access the secure shelter in the West Garage, and strongly encouraged for all riders to support theft prevention and recovery. Why Register? Registration acts as a deterrent against theft when used with the optional 529 Shield. Registration helps staff and law enforcement return lost or stolen devices. Registration is required for access to the secured, indoor bike parking area in the West Garage. E-Bike & E-Scooter Requirements Devices with electric motors must have batteries certified by UL, TUV, or another Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory (NRTL). Devices without certified batteries are not eligible for secure shelter access. If certification is missing, Transportation Services will follow up to request additional details. How to Register Use the UMass Boston 529 Registration Page or download the Project 529 app . Sign up with your UMass Boston email address. Enter your device’s make, model, color, and serial number (usually near the crank or rear wheel). Select "UMass Boston" as your organization. Submit your registration. What Happens Next Transportation Services will review your registration. You’ll receive an email when your Beaconcard has been activated for indoor, secure shelter access in the West Garage. After access is confirmed, you may request a free 529 Shield. If requested, we’ll assign it to your registration and notify you when it’s ready for pickup in our office. What Is a 529 Shield? A tamper-resistant, weatherproof sticker that links your physical device to your 529 Garage registration. It supports theft deterrence and helps with recovery. The 529 Shield is optional but strongly recommended.

## E-Bike & E-Scooter Requirements
Devices with electric motors must have batteries certified by UL, TUV, or another Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory (NRTL). Devices without certified batteries are not eligible for secure shelter access. If certification is missing, Transportation Services will follow up to request additional details.

## How to Register
- Use the UMass Boston 529 Registration Page or download the Project 529 app .
- Sign up with your UMass Boston email address.
- Enter your device’s make, model, color, and serial number (usually near the crank or rear wheel).
- Select "UMass Boston" as your organization.
- Submit your registration.

## What Happens Next
- Transportation Services will review your registration.
- You’ll receive an email when your Beaconcard has been activated for indoor, secure shelter access in the West Garage.
- After access is confirmed, you may request a free 529 Shield. If requested, we’ll assign it to your registration and notify you when it’s ready for pickup in our office.

## What Is a 529 Shield?
A tamper-resistant, weatherproof sticker that links your physical device to your 529 Garage registration. It supports theft deterrence and helps with recovery.
The 529 Shield is optional but strongly recommended.

## Riding Responsibly on Campus
To ensure a safe and enjoyable environment for everyone, UMass Boston has established clear guidelines for riding and parking on campus. Following these helps keep pathways clear and ensures access for all. Key Guidelines: Ride Safely: Always wear a helmet, yield to pedestrians, and follow traffic rules. Park Smart: Use designated racks or secure shelters. Avoid parking on sidewalks or blocking pathways to prevent your bike from being removed. Charge at Designated Stations: E-bike and e-scooter charging is currently available at the West Garage bike shelter only. Devices must be registered through Project 529 and have NRTL-certified batteries. Register Your Ride: Access secure parking by registering with Project 529.
